To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the stability region of a single-hop queueing network under channel uncertainty with known mismatch statistics is the convex hull of the stability regions with perfect channel knowledge; (ii) a back-pressure type policy is throughput optimal for the case with known mismatch statistics, and (iii) for the case when the mismatch statistics are unknown, the joint channel learning and scheduling policy proposed is throughput optimal with an associated tradeoff in the packet delay.

(i) the stability region of the network can be characterized under imperfect channel estimator statistics and a back-pressure type policy can be used to achieve it; and (ii) the stability region can be arbitrarily closed to the optimal one by using a joint channel learning and scheduling policy with a trade-off in average packet delay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of problems in wireless networks that arise due to the interaction between imperfect estimation of channel statistics and scheduling policies.
scheduling and rate adaptation in wireless networks where the channel estimates are imperfect.
scheduling in queueing networks under imperfect channel estimation and the associated trade-offs between throughput optimality, packet delay and the amount of feedback required.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed joint channel learning and scheduling scheme achieves the best performance among all possible scheduling policies, with a small penalty in the average packet delays.

we have proposed a novel joint learning and scheduling framework for time-varying wireless networks and have shown that our proposed policy is throughput optimal under the assumption that the statistics of the estimation mismatch is known.

, in the presence of imperfect channel-estimation, the back-pressure policy remains throughput optimal, but the delay is not optimal, and a joint channel learning and scheduling policy is needed to obtain a delay performance that is arbitrarily close to the delay performance of a genie-aided system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in a single-hop wireless network, a joint channel learning and scheduling policy is throughput-optimal and can have a delay performance arbitrarily close to that of a policy with perfect channel estimates.
we propose a joint channel learning and scheduling policy that can be applied for both cases, with the optimal policy for the former case being a special case of the latter.

we provide a framework to study the stability of networks with rate ad aptation under channel estimation uncertainty and propose a scheduling policy that is throughput optimal for the former and has a stability region close to the network capacity region for the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the network stability region can be recovered with an adaptive policy that can be implemented with only a single channel estimator at each transmitter.
the scheduling policy should adapt not only to the channel state but also to the channel estimator statistics.
scheduling with rate adaptation is feasible in networks with imperfect channel estimators and the performance is only marginally impacted by the inaccuracies of the estimators.
